items.prompt: Two angles of a triangle are 40° and 75°. What is the third angle?

figure.alt: A triangle with two angles marked 40° and 75°. The third angle is unknown.

options.why: 115° is 40° + 75°. The three angles add up to 180°.

hints: The angles in a triangle always add up to the same amount.
The three angles of a triangle add up to 180°.
First add the two angles you know.
items.explanation: The angles of a triangle add up to 180°. 40° + 75° = 115°, so the third angle is 180° - 115° = 65°.

items.prompt: A square has sides of 10 cm. A triangle is drawn using one side of the square and the midpoint of the opposite side. What is the area of the triangle?

Area of a triangle = base × height ÷ 2.
items.explanation: The triangle has a base of 10 cm and a height of 10 cm. Its area is 10 × 10 ÷ 2 = 50 cm², half of the square.

Both rows are split at the same place, so the right part is always 1.5 times the left.

options.why: 60° is the angle in each of the 6 triangles at the centre.

items.explanation: A hexagon splits into 4 triangles, so its angles add up to 4 × 180° = 720°. Shared equally by 6 angles, each is 720° ÷ 6 = 120°.

items.prompt: A box is 4 cm long, 3 cm wide and 2 cm tall. What is the total area of its six faces?

figure.label: 4 cm × 3 cm × 2 cm
figure.alt: A cuboid 4 cm long, 3 cm wide and 2 cm tall.

hints: The faces come in 3 matching pairs.
The pairs are 4 by 3, 4 by 2 and 3 by 2.
Find the area of one face from each pair, then double the total.
items.explanation: The three different faces have areas 4 × 3 = 12, 4 × 2 = 8 and 3 × 2 = 6. Each appears twice, so the total is 2 × (12 + 8 + 6) = 52 cm².

items.prompt: A rectangle has a perimeter of 40 cm. Its length is 4 cm more than its width. What is its area?
hints: Half the perimeter is one length plus one width.
Length + width = 20 cm, and length - width = 4 cm.
Take away the 4 cm difference and share the rest equally.
items.explanation: Length + width = 20 cm. Taking away the difference of 4 leaves 16, so the width is 8 cm and the length is 12 cm. The area is 12 × 8 = 96 cm².

items.prompt: What is the smaller angle between the hands of a clock at 3:40?

figure.alt: A clock showing 3:40. The minute hand points to 8. The hour hand is two thirds of the way from 3 to 4.

hints: The minute hand at 40 minutes points to 8.
In 60 minutes the hour hand moves 30°, so in 40 minutes it moves 20°.
Measure each hand's angle from 12.
items.explanation: From 12, the minute hand is at 8 × 30° = 240°. The hour hand is at 3 × 30° + 20° = 110°. The angle between them is 240° - 110° = 130°.

items.prompt: A square and an equilateral triangle have the same perimeter. Each side of the triangle is 16 cm. What is the area of the square?

items.explanation: The perimeter is 3 × 16 = 48 cm. Each side of the square is 48 ÷ 4 = 12 cm, so its area is 12 × 12 = 144 cm².

items.prompt: A garden is 10 m long and 8 m wide. A path 1 m wide goes all the way around the outside of the garden. What is the area of the path, in square metres?

The new length and width are each 2 m more.

items.explanation: With the path the rectangle is 12 m by 10 m, area 120 m². The garden is 10 × 8 = 80 m². The path is 120 - 80 = 40 m².

mark: What is the area of the path, in square metres?

solution.say: With the path the rectangle is 12 m by 10 m, area 120 m².

items.prompt: A square of side 8 cm is cut into two rectangles by one straight cut. One rectangle has a perimeter of 28 cm. What is the area of the other rectangle, in cm²?
hints: A cut parallel to a side makes two rectangles, each 8 cm long.
Let one rectangle have width w. Its perimeter is 2 × (8 + w).
2 × (8 + w) = 28 gives w. The other width is 8 - w.
items.explanation: Both rectangles are 8 cm long. 2 × (8 + w) = 28 gives w = 6. The other rectangle has width 8 - 6 = 2 and area 8 × 2 = 16 cm².

mark: What is the area of the other rectangle, in cm²?

solution.say: The other rectangle has width 8 - 6 = 2 and area 8 × 2 = 16 cm².
